submission.natural_language_explanation: This (negative) pole is the default-on side of a layer-0 entertainment-domain gate: it fires in a graded way (up to ~0.17) on ordinary, non-media tokens at any sentence position, and shuts off completely when the current token is a film/TV/entertainment word (show, film, movie, drama, Netflix, watched, characters...), handing the neuron to its sparse positive pole, which detects and boosts that same vocabulary. The off-state is domain-driven, not frequency- or function-word-driven: common media words ('show', 'film') silence it while rare ordinary words ('museum', 'truck') drive it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Quarterly warehouse inventory reconciliation memo for period ending September 30. Supervisors counted every pallet in aisles four through eleven during scheduled shutdown hours. Each forklift operator logged movements through handheld scanners linked directly toward central ledger software. Clerks compared physical counts against purchase orders, packing slips, invoices, plus freight manifests received from regional carriers. Discrepancies under two percent triggered automatic recounts by independent teams assigned randomly each morning. Damaged cartons were photographed, weighed, documented, then moved toward quarantine cages pending vendor credit approval. Perishable goods nearing expiration dates received priority stickers before redistribution among retail outlets across three counties. Supervisors verified thermometer logs inside refrigerated zones twice daily, noting deviations beyond allowed thresholds immediately. Payroll records for overtime hours were cross-checked against badge swipes at dock entrances. Maintenance crews serviced conveyor belts, dock levelers, hydraulic lifts, plus battery chargers according to posted schedules. Safety inspectors tested alarms, sprinklers, extinguishers, emergency lighting throughout stairwells, corridors, loading bays without exception. Auditors sampled two hundred cartons randomly, confirming labels matched contents, quantities, lot numbers exactly. Variances above tolerance required written explanations signed by both shift leads plus operations manager. Obsolete packaging materials were recycled through certified vendors providing weight tickets for every trailer load. Fuel usage for yard tractors was reconciled against delivery logs maintained by dispatch office staff. Insurance certificates for third-party haulers were reviewed, updated, filed alphabetically inside locked cabinets upstairs. Training attendance sheets documented forklift certification renewals completed before regulatory deadlines approached. Customer returns were sorted by reason codes, inspected thoroughly, restocked promptly whenever condition allowed resale under policy guidelines. Finance staff accrued reserves for shrinkage based upon three-year rolling averages adjusted seasonally. Auditors concluded controls operated effectively throughout period, noting minor housekeeping items already remediated by warehouse leadership, rating overall inventory accuracy at ninety-nine point one percent, deeming site fully compliant. Additional cycle counts scheduled during October will focus upon high-value electronics locked inside caged enclosures monitored continuously via cameras. Procurement staff renegotiated corrugated cardboard contracts securing eight percent savings while maintaining quality specifications demanded by automated packing machinery. Human resources posted updated shift bids allowing seniority-based selection before holiday volume increases expected late November. Executives praised steady improvement across accuracy metrics, authorized capital expenditure for additional racking, lighting upgrades, expanded break room facilities requested repeatedly through employee feedback surveys collected anonymously each quarter.
